A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DREAM and the same FOL theorem-proving benchmark. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original theorem-proving results, component ablations, strategy-diversity experiments, and an evaluation with background axioms removed.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds annotation agreement, computational-budget comparisons, dataset-construction statistics, and quantitative error analysis.

M1.justification: The axiom-driven diversification and sub-proposition feedback procedures, Equations (2)–(6), and Appendix A pseudocode are unchanged. The new axiom-tree illustration explains the existing construction rather than introducing a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 324 TPTP-Revised and 123 manually collected problems, domains, and axiom-removal scenario. The new audits and budget comparisons use existing coverage. Table 7's source-total correction from 629 to 627 matches the unchanged category counts and does not establish a dataset change.

E2.justification: Repeated sampling and Subgoal remain the comparators in the corresponding benchmark and background-restriction experiments; the motivation comparisons also remain unchanged. The new computational-budget experiments reuse Subgoal without introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation design with LLM-call and token accounting and a separate comparison capped at 17 calls, alongside the retained ten-iteration setting. It also introduces independent validation of 40 problems, split equally between the two corpora, and an error-classification procedure using DeepSeek-V3 and excluding singleton categories.

E4.justification: New Appendices C–F examine dataset reliability, construction attrition, computational efficiency under iteration and call budgets, and the distribution of proof failures. These substantially broaden the supplementary analyses beyond v1's retained component ablations, background-removal experiment, and qualitative cases.

E5.justification: Appendix C/Table 8 newly reports statistical annotation reliability through independent expert judgments and problem-wise agreement. Neither version provides repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests for theorem-proving performance.

E6.justification: The original main results remain unchanged, but Tables 8–12 add substantial results: 82.5% annotation agreement, construction yields, resource consumption, error frequencies, and 17-call accuracy of 11.6% for DREAM versus 6.5% for Subgoal. Table 7 corrects 629 to 627. New Table 10 also contains unexplained differences from retained results, including Subgoal's manual-dataset score of 29.1% versus 27.6% in Table 3; these are not established same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical objective, combinatorial definitions, and feedback equations are unchanged. The added axiom-tree example illustrates the existing formulation without adding a theoretical guarantee, proof, or revised mathematical assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about advancing mathematical FOL reasoning, DREAM's two components, gains of 0.6%–6.4%, and the 447-theorem dataset. The additional evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets annotation agreement as supporting dataset reliability and the call-budget comparison as evidence of greater utility per call. Appendix F adds a concrete limitation involving syntactic and type-level failures and suggests syntax-aware decoding or correction. The original mechanism explanations and applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, intermediate translation and optimization statistics, and call/token consumption information. It also identifies the auxiliary error classifier. These expand access and technical documentation; the original implementation settings and translation prompt are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds connections to autoformalization work by Yang, Zhang, and Lu, cites Zheng et al. for annotation agreement, and adds reasoning-pattern and alignment references in future-work discussion. Section 2 and the central novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely retained. Local wording corrections, revised author-role annotations, acknowledgments, expanded limitations prose, and additional appendix subsections produce a limited structural and editorial revision rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displayed evidence through five new tables covering validation, construction, computational comparisons, and errors, plus a new axiom-tree illustration. Existing appendix examples are retained but redistributed and renumbered; Figure 4 also receives limited graphical and label adjustments.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 makes dataset construction, annotation reliability, computational cost, and failure modes more inspectable and supplies a code link. The equal-call comparison addresses a useful evaluation gap. However, unexplained score discrepancies between Table 10 and Tables 2–3, plus 17 calls in the accompanying text versus 18 in Table 10, limit confidence in the new efficiency evidence. The net gain is useful but limited.
